_source: Hand-curated from internal/gateway/connector setup paths and hook profiles, cli/defenseclaw/inventory/hook_contracts.json, the native Windows setup contracts, and the OpenShell sandbox artifacts (internal/gateway/connector/*_sandbox.go, internal/openshell/harness). Re-extract on every connector, hook-contract, or platform-support change.
_order: By adoption / popularity — mirrors the hero rotation (lib/hero-connectors.ts) and the docs nav (content/docs/connectors/index(hook-connectors)/meta.json).

connectors.label: Claude Code
connectors.windowsNote: Native executable hooks are supported on Windows x64; WSL is outside this connector contract.
connectors.summary: Native lifecycle hooks and approval on hosts; OpenTelemetry export only in isolated OpenShell.
connectors.hilt: Claude Code supports native PreToolUse ask prompts. CRITICAL findings still block; HIGH findings can pause for approval.
connectors.notes: Host installs use hooks with no native OTLP exporter or proxy data path. Isolated OpenShell adds native logs and metrics. Host observability and PreToolUse deny decisions flow through the hook bus.

connectors.label: Codex
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses the packaged PowerShell bridge and hook executable.
connectors.summary: Config hooks on hosts; native OpenTelemetry only in isolated OpenShell; turn-completion bridge in Secure Client and OpenShell.
connectors.hilt: Codex has no native ask surface here; confirm becomes an alert/systemMessage with raw_action preserved. The TUI can review the event but cannot resume it.
connectors.notes: Host installs use hooks without native OTel. Secure Client and isolated OpenShell use a turn-completion bridge; only OpenShell renders native OTel. Hook-only connector — no proxy data path and no DefenseClaw subprocess sandbox or command shims.

connectors.label: OpenClaw
connectors.windowsNote: The OpenClaw integration requires the guardrail proxy, which DefenseClaw does not host on native Windows.
connectors.summary: Reference proxy with bundled fetch interception and before-tool-call enforcement.
connectors.hilt: OpenClaw supports DefenseClaw approval prompts for tool actions. Approvals reach chat-origin sessions via the bundled plugin.
connectors.notes: Reference proxy connector — full data-path interception, command-shim subprocess enforcement, plugin-mediated HITL.

connectors.label: Cursor
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses the managed PowerShell adapter and packaged hook executable.
connectors.summary: User hooks with bounded inspection and event-native deny decisions.

sandbox.unverifiedReason: The Cursor Agent CLI needs a Cursor account (CURSOR_API_KEY or cursor-agent login) before any agent turn

connectors.hilt: DefenseClaw does not enable Cursor native human approval. Confirm verdicts remain attributed alerts and cannot resume the original hook call.
connectors.notes: Native Windows setup is supported. Validation version/date/run metadata remains empty and live=false. The connector writes only ~/.cursor/hooks.json. Action mode returns Cursor's documented native deny response on supported pre-action events and writes failClosed=true; observe returns allow/would-block and writes failClosed=false. Cursor merges conflicts Enterprise > Team > Project > User, but exposes no safe API for detecting an actual higher-priority conflict, so DefenseClaw reports that limitation and does not infer a conflict. The direct native adapter and all documented event schemas remain active for bounded inspection, including subagentStart and post/result fields. Agent CLI version evidence is separate from the event payload's Cursor application/Desktop cursor_version. Local inventory covers documented MCP, recursive skill and compatibility roots, .cursor/rules/**/*.mdc, root/nested AGENTS.md, local plugins, and project/user compatibility subagents; multi-root, cloud, marketplace/team/private, dynamic, and effective same-name sources remain unverified.

connectors.label: Hermes
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses a direct, shell-free hook executable invocation.
connectors.summary: Native lifecycle hooks with valid-JSON pre-tool blocking.
connectors.hilt: Hermes has no native human-approval surface; confirm verdicts are recorded and alerted but cannot pause or resume the hook.
connectors.notes: Native Windows setup is supported; validation metadata remains empty and live=false. The connector covers one resolved default HERMES_HOME only and rejects named or multiplex profiles. It stages all 23 Hermes v0.19 hooks in config.yaml while preserving hooks_auto_accept, and transactionally owns only exact DefenseClaw event/command approvals in shell-hooks-allowlist.json. Running hosts cache callbacks, so registration and revocation remain pending reload; Windows teardown writes a direct-native disabled tombstone for stale callbacks. Only valid synchronous pre_tool_call block JSON vetoes a tool; pre_llm_call may inject context and pre_verify may continue a bounded verification loop. Other events are audit-only where the official shell parser proves no effect, and all failures remain open. The command is a directly quoted absolute native defenseclaw-hook.exe argv parsed by shlex.split and run with shell=False; there is no shell fallback and Hermes's PortableGit terminal is outside the integration. Bounded default-profile inventory covers MCP, local/external skills, SOUL.md, built-in/provider memory, and bundled/Nix/user/pip plugins; project-conditional, named-profile, and managed/ProgramData/cloud/MDM sources remain unverified.

connectors.label: OpenCode
connectors.windowsNote: Direct native Windows x64 execution is supported for the admitted WinGet CLI.
connectors.summary: Auto-loaded bridge plugin with tool-execution blocking.
connectors.hilt: No native human-approval surface; blocks by throwing in the bridge plugin's tool.execute.before. confirm verdicts fall back to allow.
connectors.notes: Native Windows setup is supported; validation metadata remains empty and live=false. Governed by a DefenseClaw JS bridge plugin auto-loaded from OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/defenseclaw.js or the default ~/.config/opencode/plugins/defenseclaw.js (no opencode.json edit). tool.execute.before POSTs to /api/v1/opencode/hook and throws new Error(reason) to abort the tool on a block decision; tool.execute.after is best-effort observe-only. Fail-closed applies only to the awaited before hook: the bridge throws there when the gateway is unreachable and FAIL_MODE=closed.

connectors.label: Amp
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses the owner-only TypeScript system-policy plugin.
connectors.summary: Synchronous policy plugin with five lifecycle events and native confirmation.

sandbox.unverifiedReason: Amp needs an Amp account API key (AMP_API_KEY) for every run

connectors.hilt: Amp can ask in the active foreground thread during tool.call and before a tool.result reaches the model. Denial, a background thread, or unavailable plugin UI rejects the call or withholds the result rather than silently allowing it.
connectors.notes: A managed TypeScript plugin at ~/.config/amp/plugins/defenseclaw.ts forwards session.start, agent.start, tool.call, tool.result, and agent.end to /api/v1/amp/hook. tool.call is synchronously enforceable before execution, and tool.result can be replaced before model delivery but cannot undo completed side effects. Execute mode must use --plugin-ready-timeout 30 for lifecycle capture and guard readiness. Amp's reported custom-agent definition or built-in mode enriches Agent360 without being treated as a stable ID, request trace, or parent link. Delegation tools such as Task and oracle are governed at launch, and any emitted child-thread events remain independently correlated unless Amp supplies canonical parent evidence. No native OTLP or W3C traceparent channel is advertised.

connectors.label: GitHub Copilot CLI
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses Copilot CLI's PowerShell hook field.
connectors.summary: Global or workspace hooks that block before a tool runs.
connectors.hilt: Copilot CLI confirmations block because its hook does not prove an approval prompt is available; VS Code Local uses its separate native ask.
connectors.notes: Native Windows setup is supported. Provider authentication remains required; HITL and official-client live evidence are unverified and unclaimed, validation metadata remains empty, and live=false. Global hooks live under ~/.copilot/hooks by default with optional workspace hooks under <workspace>/.github/hooks.

connectors.label: Antigravity
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 uses the packaged PowerShell hook launcher.
connectors.summary: Five lifecycle hooks, with documented native ask on PreToolUse.
connectors.hilt: Antigravity documents native ask on PreToolUse only. DefenseClaw sends force_ask, which ignores cached Always Allow grants, never plain ask. DefenseClaw does not claim that this response overrides permission-bypass flags without persisted official-client evidence.
connectors.notes: Native Windows setup is supported. Provider authentication remains required; HITL and official-client live evidence are unverified and unclaimed, validation metadata remains empty, and live=false. DefenseClaw's v2 contract registers all five documented Antigravity lifecycle events (PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostInvocation, Stop) in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json with their vendor-specific direct-list or matcher-group shapes. Only synchronous PreToolUse exposes documented hard deny and native ask decisions; invocation events are context-transform surfaces, PostToolUse is observe-only, and DefenseClaw returns allow for Stop rather than claiming stop blocking. MCP read/write uses ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json and <workspace>/.agents/mcp_config.json. AgentSkills folder form is read/write at ~/.gemini/config/skills and <workspace>/.agents/skills. Plugins live at ~/.gemini/config/plugins or <workspace>/.agents/plugins; the CLI staging path is also discovered. Rules and standalone or plugin-contained agents remain discovery/scan only.

connectors.label: Devin
connectors.windowsNote: Native Windows x64 supports the admitted same-user Devin CLI and system-PowerShell bridge.
connectors.summary: Native lifecycle hooks for Devin CLI and Devin Desktop's Devin Local agent, with a source-reviewed 3000.4.25 contract.

sandbox.unverifiedReason: The Devin CLI needs a Devin account login (devin auth login, a browser or pasted-token flow) before any agent turn

connectors.hilt: Can block documented events but has no native resumable human-approval surface; confirm verdicts fall back explicitly.
connectors.notes: The native devin-hooks-v1 contract registers eight lifecycle events in user config.json or project .devin/hooks.v1.json. Exit 2 blocks; every other hook error fails open. Session and turn correlation use session_id and prompt_id, but Devin publishes no stable per-tool invocation ID, so paired tool state is detection-only. Restricted Mode disables hooks and agents. Devin Desktop's default Devin Local agent shares the Devin CLI hook config; Devin Desktop 3.9.19 removed the legacy Cascade agent, which earlier builds run uncovered. The separate native devin acp entry point is cataloged for the shared DefenseClaw ACP guard but is not certified; cloud Devin, proxy transport, native OTLP, and managed higher-layer enforcement are excluded, and plugin hooks are checked only by the standalone foreign-hook guard.

connectors.label: Kiro
connectors.windowsNote: The defenseclaw-acp stdio mediator is platform-neutral; packaged Windows x64 evidence is required before release certification.
connectors.summary: Kiro IDE and Kiro CLI share native hooks; ACP adds an optional mediated stdio path.
connectors.hilt: Kiro has no native ask verdict; policy confirms are recorded and downgraded to alerts. ACP permission requests stay native client interactions and may be denied before the client displays them.
connectors.notes: Native hooks are the enforcement boundary and are workspace-scoped: Kiro loads only .kiro/hooks/*.json relative to the project root, so a project-local defenseclaw.json is required and the user-global ~/.kiro/hooks copy is inert. A CLI 2.x defenseclaw agent carries the same hooks for kiro-cli 2.x. defenseclaw-acp remains an optional second surface configured with `defenseclaw acp setup --agent kiro`. Known limit: the sandbox image still pins kiro-cli 2.24.1, below the 2.27.1 host floor. Its launcher runs only the V2 agent engine and refuses --v3, so the V3 non-interactive path that loads no hooks before 2.27.1 cannot run there; the pin moves with a newly pinned, hash-verified build.

connectors.label: ZeptoClaw
connectors.windowsNote: The ZeptoClaw integration requires the guardrail proxy, which DefenseClaw does not host on native Windows.
connectors.summary: API base redirect through the DefenseClaw proxy with response scanning.
connectors.hilt: ZeptoClaw has no native ask surface; confirm uses its explicit fallback with raw_action preserved for TUI/audit review. There is no resumable approval.
connectors.notes: api_base redirect into the DefenseClaw proxy plus response-scan.
